statements.t: We expect overall spending on health care to continue to grow in the future, due to inflation, medical technology and pharmaceutical advancement, regulatory requirements, demographic trends in the population and national interest in health and well-being.

To price our health care benefits, products and services, we start with our view of expected future costs, including medical care patterns, the mix and health status of people served, inflation and labor market dynamics.
We expect broad-based competition to continue as the industry adapts to individual and employer needs.

As expected and contemplated in our benefits design and pricing, we have continued to observe increased care patterns, health care unit costs and the intensity of services delivered, which are driven by increases in provider pricing and additional services bundled per visit.
Additionally, we decide annually on a county-by-county basis where we will offer Medicare Advantage plans.

Given the significant portion of our portfolio held in cash and cash equivalents, we do not anticipate fluctuations in the aggregate fair value of our financial assets to have a material impact on our liquidity or capital position.
We base our assumptions and estimates primarily on historical experience and consider known and projected trends.

dropped.t: Continued funding pressures have resulted in benefit and pricing actions, causing contraction in our Medicare Advantage membership, which we expect to continue throughout 2026.
